svg.text: VIBEGUARD: PHYSICAL BREADBOARD & DESK WIRING GUIDE
EXACT STEP-BY-STEP PIN CONNECTION & COMPONENT LAYOUT — MB102 SOLDERLESS BREADBOARD

g.text: WIRING METHOD: Female-to-Male (F2M) Jumpers off-board (Full breadboard area available)
POWER RAILS: Red = +3.3V Regulated (AMS1117), Blue = GND (0V)
MANDATORY RULE: Motor 12V supply is 100% ISOLATED. Never connect 12V GND to Breadboard GND!
5×20 mm INLINE SCREW FUSE HOLDER (1.0A FUSE)
Connected Anti-Parallel Directly Across Motor Solder Tags
N20 MICRO METAL GEAR DC MOTOR (12V 600 RPM)
STEP-BY-STEP PHYSICAL ASSEMBLY & VERIFICATION AUDIT CHECKLIST
1. Connect Red F2M wire from ESP32 3V3 pin to Breadboard Red Rail (+).
2. Connect Black F2M wire from ESP32 GND pin to Breadboard Blue Rail (-).
3. Insert 100 µF radial electrolytic capacitor directly across rails:
• Shorter lead with white minus stripe (Negative) into Blue Rail (-)
4. Insert 100 nF (104) ceramic capacitor in parallel across Red (+) and Blue (-).
5. Plug USB-C cable into PC; verify ESP32 red power LED turns ON steadily.
The ESP32 draws ~500mA transient pulses during startup and Wi-Fi bursts.
The AMS1117 LDO loop delay causes a 15µs sag without bulk capacitance.
The 100µF capacitor holds the rail above 3.10V, safely above the 2.70V brownout
detector threshold (rst:0x10), preventing endless reboot cycles.
1. Insert 5mm Common Cathode RGB LED into breadboard:
• Pin 1 (Red Anode) → Row 12 | Pin 2 (Cathode - Longest) → Row 13
• Pin 3 (Green Anode) → Row 14 | Pin 4 (Blue Anode) → Row 15
2. Wire Pin 2 (Cathode) to Blue Rail (-) with a jumper.
3. Insert 3× 330 Ω resistors in series with Red, Green, and Blue pins.
4. Connect GPIO lines from ESP32 to resistors:
• INT1 → GPIO 4 (J3-13) | VCC → Red Rail (+) | GND → Blue Rail (-)
1. 12V 2A DC Adapter plugs into 5.5×2.1mm DC Barrel Jack Screw Terminal.
2. Route Positive (+12V) through KCD1 Rocker Switch (inline power cut).
3. Route Switch output through 5×20mm Inline Fuse Holder (1.0A fuse).
4. Solder 1N4007 Diode anti-parallel directly across N20 motor tags:
5. Connect DC Jack (-) GND directly to Motor (-) terminal.
NEVER connect 12V Motor Ground to ESP32 or Breadboard Ground!
Motor commutator sparks and back-EMF ripple circulating in logic ground
will corrupt SPI readings and risk destroying host computer USB ports.
Mechanical baseplate transmits vibration; zero electrical return is needed.
